rawRetro.summary: Repair round 5: the six reported failures in the after-sales service module are fixed. The work-order resolution dialog now closes on success, so Reject no longer opens a stale Submit dialog and cannot duplicate a transition. The DOCX preview is time-bounded and reports a real error instead of hanging, and a corrupt image is rejected at upload and at preview. The authenticated shell mounts the in-app notification provider with an unread bell and an authorized inbox route, and resolution and rejection now notify the people who act on them. The overdue-reminder plan scans un-closed overdue work orders, counts accepted deliveries, refuses to run while disabled, and the dialogs use the application date picker. List search filters on type, Enter and blur with a clear control. API keys are issued and revoked for the integration account through the API Keys plugin (never for the signed-in administrator), and an external self-status read was added. Scoped typecheck, eslint, Prettier and the affected service, file-preview, date-picker, locale and route tests pass.

blockers.title: operations.ts truncated mid-method by a chunked here-doc append
blockers.symptom: server/providers/service/operations.ts: SyntaxError: '}' expected. (2418:1); the file ended at `async createManual(actor: ServiceActor, input: Row): Promise` with no body or closing brace, and `format:auto` exited 2 in 0.90s.
blockers.rootCause: The implementation agent wrote the large service file through repeated `cat >> ... <<'CHUNK'` appends. One chunk was cut off (the shell logged `warning: here-document delimited by end-of-file (wanted 'CHUNK')`) and the agent's own response then hit the model output-token cap mid-thought (`stopReason: length`, thinking "Oops, my heredoc"), so the truncation was never noticed or repaired.
blockers.resolution: Read the migration and seed as the schema source of truth, removed the truncated fragment, and re-wrote the missing tail: attachment read/register/detach/resolve, manual CRUD and indexing, external-platform intake with eventId idempotency, integration status, and the dashboard/engineer-load queries. Cross-checked every `row.*`, `values.*`, `input.*` and `filter.*('col')` reference in the file against the migration's columns and fixed the remaining drifts.

blockers.title: Service code and migration disagreed on columns and column types
blockers.symptom: Latent in the same file: work orders read and wrote `acceptNoteStatus` and `acceptanceRunId` and shares read and wrote `grantedAt`, none of which existed in the migration; and `resolutionSubmittedById`/`closedById` were declared `integer` while the service and seed write the string account id.
blockers.rootCause: The truncated file was an incomplete draft, so its later methods and the migration were written at different times and were never reconciled against each other.
blockers.resolution: Added `acceptNoteStatus` (string, default `pending`), `acceptanceRunId` and `grantedAt` to the service schema migration, and changed `resolutionSubmittedById` / `closedById` to `string(64)` to match the account-id convention used by `createdById`. The migration was untracked and unmerged and had not been applied to any persistent database, so it was corrected in place; `db apply` was then run against a fresh SQLite database to confirm the schema, the six seeded work orders and the full demo data set apply cleanly.

blockers.title: The service feature is not registered, so no business page or endpoint is reachable
blockers.symptom: server/providers/index.ts and server/routes/index.ts export empty arrays, client/routes.ts declares only the home and auth pages, and there are no jobs or permission seeds. Only the migration, the seed and the six `server/providers/service/*` internals exist, so a running application shows only the homepage and the demo data is unreachable.
blockers.rootCause: The registration, route, page, job, permission and AI/Scheduler wiring were never written: the implementation agent ran out of output tokens and then its context-overflow recovery failed (`compaction_start/overflow` -> `Context overflow recovery failed`), ending the run before the remaining files were produced.
blockers.resolution: Registered the service provider (`app/service`) with permission-set creation, demo-account provisioning, acceptance-workflow materialization and Scheduler target/schedule registration; added the `/api/service/*` route module and the guarded file-repository exposure; declared the eleven client pages and their navigation group in client/routes.ts with zh/en keys; added the source-managed `work-order-acceptance` Workflow whose run modules write the acceptance note. Verified at runtime: sign-in, every list endpoint, the accept -> workflow -> note -> in-app inbox flow, attachment round-trip, and 401/403 gating.

blockers.title: Stale database schema: creating a work order returned 409 `Field "acceptNoteStatus" does not exist`
blockers.symptom: POST /api/service/work-orders answered 409 CONFLICT `Could not allocate a work-order number: Field "acceptNoteStatus" does not exist.` against the persistent development SQLite database, while every read endpoint worked.
blockers.rootCause: The applied database had been migrated from an earlier revision of `202611010001_service_schema` that predated `acceptNoteStatus` and `acceptanceRunId`; the file was edited afterwards, so its recorded checksum no longer matched its source and the already-recorded migration was not replayed. `db redo` could not repair it because the whole database is one batch containing an irreversible plugin migration.
blockers.resolution: Added the conditional corrective migration `202611010003_service_acceptance_columns`, whose `shouldRun` reads the physical table through the connection's schema inspector and only alters a database that is actually missing the columns, so it is a no-op on a fresh database. `pnpm nocobase db apply` executed it as batch 2 and the columns now exist; creating a work order returns 200. The decision is pinned by tests/logic/service-acceptance-migration.test.ts and the DDL was exercised against the real database by `db apply`.

blockers.title: Optional enum filter compared against `undefined`, so the route's `?? ''` default became an empty enum value
blockers.symptom: GET /api/service/work-orders answered an error because the domain pushed a `priority` filter built from the empty string the route passes when the query parameter is absent; the other list endpoints were unaffected because their optional strings defaulted differently.
blockers.rootCause: The domain treated the presence of the `priority` key as intent to filter and did not normalise or validate the value, while the route always supplies the key with a `?? ''` fallback. A unit test over pure helpers could not see this because it only fails when a repository compiles the filter.
blockers.resolution: `listWorkOrders` now normalises the value with the shared `str` helper and only pushes an enum filter when it is non-empty, validating against `WORK_ORDER_PRIORITIES` and returning a 400 for an unknown value. Regression cases in tests/logic/service-operations-queries.test.ts assert that the empty default pushes no filter and that an unknown priority is rejected.

blockers.title: Inspection generator bounded a `date` column with a datetime string
blockers.symptom: POST /api/service/inspections/generate answered an error / logged `Invalid date value for Field "nextInspectionDate"` instead of creating due inspection tasks.
blockers.rootCause: `generateDailyInspections` filtered `nextInspectionDate` with a `before('<planDate>T23:59:59+08:00')` bound, but the collection declares that field as `date`, and the repository's temporal validator refuses a datetime string for a date column. A `before` bound would also skip a device due exactly on the plan date.
blockers.resolution: The bound is now the date-only plan value with an inclusive `notAfter`, so a device due exactly today is included and the validator accepts the comparison. The local filter-operator interface was extended with the `notBefore`/`notAfter` operators the real builder already provides. A regression case asserts the emitted filter uses a date-only value.

blockers.title: Upload capability and domain rule disagreed about who may attach evidence
blockers.symptom: A supervisor saw the attachment upload control because `capabilities().canUploadAttachment` is enabled for a manager, but POST /api/service/work-orders/:id/attachments answered 404 `Work order #7 was not found` for that same supervisor, because the domain allowed only the assigned engineer.
blockers.rootCause: The two rules were written from one helper (`handler = isManager || isAssignee`) but the domain method applied a stricter `isAssignee` check, so the page offered an action the domain refused. The uploader is recorded in `uploaderId`, so allowing a supervisor does not attribute their upload to the engineer.
blockers.resolution: `registerAttachment` now permits the assigned engineer or a supervisor, matching the capability flag (a temporary collaborator still may not). The method comment states the rule. Regression cases cover the supervisor, the unrelated engineer and the extension check.

blockers.title: The provider called Scheduler read methods the public token type does not declare, so pnpm build failed and the browser QA saw the blank template
blockers.symptom: pnpm build failed at the Build server step with TS2339: Property 'list' / 'listOccurrences' does not exist on type 'SchedulerService' (plus implicit-any and Set<unknown> follow-on errors) in server/providers/service/provider.ts. Because the production dist was not rebuilt, the browser acceptance (NODE_ENV=production pnpm start) served a stale client, so the B01-B12 defects all reported a blank Default Template homepage with only a Home menu entry and no business pages.
blockers.rootCause: The provider imported schedulerServiceToken from the public @nocobase/app-plugin-scheduler/server/tokens entry, whose declared type only carries the registration surface (registerTarget/defineSchedule). The service actually bound to that token is the plugin's own concrete implementation, which also exposes list and listOccurrences — the same methods its management routes call — but the public declaration hides them, so the calls did not typecheck.
blockers.resolution: Described the Scheduler read surface locally (SchedulerReadService with list/listOccurrences and minimal record shapes) and cast the resolved token to it, so the reads resolve at runtime without a deep import of the plugin's unexported internal path. Confirmed with pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.server.json --noEmit (clean), a full pnpm build (Build complete), and a production pnpm start driven by headless Chrome: the sidebar shows After-sales service with Service dashboard, Work orders, Equipment, Customers, Inspections, Repair knowledge, Equipment manuals, AI service assistant and Device integration, and GET /api/service/schedules, /dashboard, /work-orders, /customers, /equipment, /knowledge all return 200 with seeded data.

blockers.title: A Workflow run module imported application tokens by relative path, so the packed artifact was not relocatable
blockers.symptom: At boot in the production build the Workflow loader threw `Cannot find module '.../storage/workflows/providers/service/tokens.js'` (node key `acceptNormal`); the run modules had been copied into the artifact store but their relative imports still pointed at the application source tree.
blockers.rootCause: The `server/workflows/work-order-acceptance/server/` run modules imported app-local code (`provider.js`, `tokens.js`) by relative path. The artifact store materializes the workflow package as a copy under `storage/workflows/<key>/<digest>`, so relative imports out of the copied package root do not resolve, and only bare-package (framework) tokens are relocatable. Materializing the app tree too would have made the artifact depend on this application's build layout.
blockers.resolution: Removed the run modules and reduced the workflow to core-only built-in nodes (a `Condition` and a `Terminate`) that contain no application imports, then moved the acceptance-note effect into the application: `ServiceOperations.runAcceptance` computes the note with a pure `acceptanceNote()` helper, calls `completeAcceptance` synchronously, and only then optionally triggers the workflow for its side effects. The effect therefore cannot be lost to a Workflow outage. The materialized artifact digest is `f8da6acfbb2b57b15a5a9c7978cdac2ccf05c13f55ed6cecbfe26789168e9d12` and the boot log reports `acceptance workflow is materialized and enabled`.

blockers.title: Enabling a Workflow by its current flag mismatched the materialized artifact, duplicating runs
blockers.symptom: The acceptance Workflow could be enabled against the source form while a different digest was materialized, so triggers either failed to find the artifact or ran alongside a stale one.
blockers.rootCause: `WorkflowService` records versions by content digest and materializes by digest; enabling via the `current` row selected a row whose digest was not the one on disk, and the development source and production build materialize different digests.
blockers.resolution: `server/providers/service/provider.ts` now enables the workflow by the exact materialized `artifact.digest` and, inside one transaction, clears the sibling `current`/`enabled` flags so exactly one version is active. The digest published in the startup log is the one that must match.

blockers.title: Work-order detail page read the wrong route parameter and requested a NaN id
blockers.symptom: Opening `/service/work-orders/1` produced `GET /api/service/work-orders/NaN` returning HTTP 400 and the page did not render the order.
blockers.rootCause: `client/pages/service/work-order-detail.tsx` read `Number(params.id)`, but the route is declared as `/service/work-orders/:workOrderId`, so `params.id` was always undefined.
blockers.resolution: Read `Number(params.workOrderId)`. The detail page now renders the order and no NaN request is issued.

blockers.title: A label used `t()` on a key that holds a translation object, so React rendered nothing
blockers.symptom: The work-order detail source label threw `Objects are not valid as a React child` (or rendered blank), because `t('service.workOrders.source')` returned the nested `source` object rather than a string.
blockers.rootCause: The locale block defines `service.workOrders.source` as an object (its values are the per-source labels), and the component passed the object to `t()` as a child.
blockers.resolution: Added a dedicated `service.workOrders.sourceLabel` string in both `client/locales/en-US.ts` and `client/locales/zh-CN.ts` and switched the component to it.

blockers.title: The AI assistant page returned 403 for every service role that could open it
blockers.symptom: `/service/assistant` rendered but the AI-employee client's `aiEmployees:list` (and `llmServices:*`, `ai:listProviderModels`) returned 403 for the manager and engineer, so the readiness surface had no data to show.
blockers.rootCause: The AI-employee plugin gates all of its settings actions behind one page grant, `{type:'page', id:'ai.settings'}`, via `requireAISettingsAccess()` in `settings-access.js`. The service permission sets granted scheduler and business pages but never `ai.settings`, and only root bypasses the check.
blockers.resolution: Granted `pageGrant('ai.settings')` to the manager permission set (the supervisor maintains the knowledge base and needs processing status) while deliberately leaving it off the engineer set, because the same page id also carries manual upload and deletion. `client/pages/service/assistant.tsx` now checks `useCan({resource:{type:'page',id:'ai.settings'},action:'access'})` and, for a caller without it, shows a supervisor-only card instead of firing the denied requests. Verified: manager `aiEmployees:list` 200 with the readiness card, engineer 403-free with the supervisor card.

blockers.title: Knowledge-base settings page failed with 404 because the legacy portal SDK resolved an API base without the mount path
blockers.symptom: `/settings/ai/knowledge-base` rendered `Unable to load this view / NocoBase request failed (404)`; the browser issued `GET /api/ai/aiKnowledgeBase:list` instead of `/main/api/ai/aiKnowledgeBase:list`.
blockers.rootCause: The knowledge-base client builds its service through the deprecated `@nocobase/app-portal-sdk`, whose `NocoBaseClient` resolves its API base at module load from `window.NOCOBASE_API_URL` and falls back to `http://127.0.0.1:13000/api`. The v3 runtime deliberately publishes nothing on `window`; the base path lives only in the served `nocobase-runtime-config` JSON (`config.api.baseURL = /main/api`).
blockers.resolution: Added `client/portal-api-url.ts` (`publishLegacyApiUrl()`), which reads the `nocobase-runtime-config` block and sets `window.NOCOBASE_API_URL`, and imported it first in `client/index.tsx` so the global exists before the knowledge-base plugin module is evaluated. Verified: the page now loads with no 404 or console error.

blockers.title: The landing page and shell still presented the template's identity instead of the application's
blockers.symptom: Browser observations reported a blank `Default Template v1.0.0-beta.50` homepage with no business menu; the sidebar footer read `AI builds freely. / NocoBase keeps it reliable.` and the header `AI application workspace`.
blockers.rootCause: The application registered its own routes and pages but never replaced the template's home component or its shell copy, so `/` was the template scaffold and the visible chrome named the template.
blockers.resolution: Rewrote `client/pages/home.tsx` into a business landing that links to every `/service/*` area, reworded `shell.workspace`/`shell.buildFreely`/`shell.reliability` to this application's wording in both locales, and made `client/layouts/components/sidebar-footer.tsx` fall back to this application's name (`t('shell.appName', {defaultValue:'Equipment after-sales service'})`) when the deployed `dist/package.json` carries no `displayName`. The two template shell tests were updated to the application's wording, keeping their mechanism assertions (language switch without remount, one active sidebar) intact.

blockers.title: Observers and engineers triggered 403s because the registration dialog mounted for callers who cannot register
blockers.symptom: On `/service/work-orders` an observer issued `GET /api/service/customers?pageSize=200` and `GET /api/service/equipment?pageSize=200`, both 403, on every page load, even though the page rendered.
blockers.rootCause: `CreateWorkOrderDialog` was always mounted and its `useLoad` fetched the customer and equipment options on mount. Registration is a manager-only action (`createWorkOrder` calls `requireManager`), so callers who hold the page only to read it were loading reference data their role is denied.
blockers.resolution: The page loads `/me` and renders the `Register` action and the dialog only when the caller's roles include `manager`. Verified: manager keeps the `New work order` button and its option load, observer and engineer see neither the button nor the dialog and issue no 403.

blockers.title: integration.tsx imported ExecutionPlansCard without using it after the plans card moved to the inspections page
blockers.symptom: eslint . --max-warnings 0 exited 1: client/pages/service/integration.tsx:70:10 error 'ExecutionPlansCard' is defined but never used. The remaining format, type and test stages still ran, so the failing gate was lint alone.
blockers.rootCause: The scheduled-plan card was moved to client/pages/service/inspections.tsx (which mounts it for managers), but integration.tsx kept the now-dead import; the file comment already stated plans live on the inspections page.
blockers.resolution: Removed the unused import from client/pages/service/integration.tsx. Scoped eslint on the file passes with --max-warnings 0 and Prettier reports the file clean; no behavior changed because the symbol was never referenced.

blockers.title: Work-order resolution dialog kept its stale label and re-posted after a success
blockers.symptom: After submitting a resolution in the same page session, 'Reject result' opened a dialog titled 'Submit resolution' and its Confirm posted to /api/service/work-orders/6/resolution, which answered 409; the close and reject dialogs also stayed open after a successful action.
blockers.rootCause: The detail page held one `dialog` state string and `act()` awaited the request but never cleared it, so the previous dialog's label and body were still bound to the open dialog and its submit handler targeted the resolution endpoint a second time. The 409 was the server correctly refusing the duplicate state transition.
blockers.resolution: `act()` in client/pages/service/work-order-detail.tsx now closes the dialog (`setDialog(null)`) after a successful action, leaving it open on failure so typed input is not lost, and then reloads the record. The open dialog therefore always matches the action the user chose and a finished transition cannot be re-submitted.

blockers.title: DOCX preview could hang on 'Loading preview' and a corrupt image was accepted without feedback
blockers.symptom: Opening a .docx attachment left the preview at 'Loading preview…' with no iframe and no error although the content request returned 200; uploading a corrupt PNG with naturalWidth 0 was accepted and produced no failure feedback.
blockers.rootCause: The Office Open XML viewer awaited the renderer and the document fetch with no time bound, so a renderer that never settled left the loading state forever with no path to an error. The image branch rendered a plain and ignored decode failure.
blockers.resolution: office-open-xml-preview.tsx now bounds both the document request (15s) and the renderer load (20s) with `withTimeout`, routing a timeout through the existing error surface, and uses a ref for `t` so the effect does not re-run on an unstable callback. file-preview-content.tsx gains an `ImagePreview` that shows a loading state, flips to a localized download fallback on `onError` or `naturalWidth === 0`, and the work-order attachment upload now rejects a zero-byte file, a photo that does not decode and a report without the ZIP `PK` signature before sending it, reporting the reason as a toast.

blockers.title: No in-app message center, unread badge, or notifications for resolution and rejection
blockers.symptom: The application had no way to open the durable in-app inbox, no unread badge in the shell, and the acceptance, resolution-submitted and rejected messages an assignee or supervisor needs could not be reached from the UI; the only inbox route was the plugin's development-only /dev page.
blockers.rootCause: The notification-in-app plugin was registered but the application never mounted its provider, declared an authenticated inbox page or put a bell in the header, and the domain only sent a notification in `completeAcceptance`: `submitResolution` and `rejectWorkOrder` changed state without telling anyone it matters to.
blockers.resolution: The authenticated shell in client/routing/app-router.tsx now mounts `NotificationInAppProvider`; a new header component reads `NotificationInAppRuntimeContext` for the unread count and links to a new authenticated, authorized `/service/messages` route that renders `NotificationInAppInbox`; the route is declared in client/routes.ts with `authz` and navigation, the page grant and page id are added to the four service permission sets, and `submitResolution` (to managers) and `rejectWorkOrder` (to the assignee) now send a durable notification through the same `notify`/`notifyManagers` path with a version-scoped idempotency key.

blockers.title: Overdue reminder plan scanned only inspections, still ran while disabled, and the date pickers closed their dialog
blockers.symptom: The overdue-reminder plan reported `reminded: 0` while overdue work orders existed; a disabled plan could still be executed through the controlled 'Run now' action; and choosing the next-inspection date or a work-order deadline with the native date input dismissed the whole dialog.
blockers.rootCause: `sendOverdueReminders` only looked at inspection tasks and counted each attempt rather than each accepted delivery, so overdue work orders were never reminded; `schedulerRunner.run` triggered the registered target without consulting `plan.enabled`; and the two dialogs used a native <input type='date'> inside a form the dialog treated as dismissible on change.
blockers.resolution: `sendOverdueReminders` scans un-closed work orders whose deadline has passed (idempotency `work-order.overdue:<id>:<day>`) in addition to the inspection half, and `notify`/`notifyAssignee` now return whether the notification service accepted the message so `reminded` counts real sends and a deduplicated delivery is not recounted. `schedulerRunner.run` refuses a switched-off plan with `status: 'skipped'`, `enabled: false` and no trigger. Both dialogs now use the application `DatePicker` (popover-based, whose button defaults to type='button') with a hidden input carrying `yyyy-MM-dd` to the FormData.

blockers.title: List search boxes did not filter until an unhandled native submit
blockers.symptom: Typing ZZZNOMATCH in the equipment or work-order list search box and pressing Enter left every row visible; the input did not filter as the user typed and had no way to clear it.
blockers.rootCause: The search input was uncontrolled and only the surrounding form's submit navigation committed it, so an Enter that did not submit the form (or a blur) never reached the query, and there was no feedback that a filter was pending.
blockers.resolution: Both list pages now use a controlled search input with a 300ms debounce, and commit on Enter (explicitly, rather than relying on form submission) and on blur; a ghost clear button resets the query and the page. Every commit resets to page 1 and updates the URL/query so the filter is durable and shareable.

blockers.title: Administrator API keys lacked the integrator role and the platform had no self-status read
blockers.symptom: A key created on the administrator's own API Keys settings page authenticates as that administrator, who holds no `service-integrator` role, so an external submit answered 403; there was no way to issue a key for the integration account; and `GET /api/service/external/repairs/:id` returned the SPA fallback because no route existed.
blockers.rootCause: The integration page told reviewers to create the key in Settings, where the plugin issues it for the signed-in administrator rather than the integration seat, and the domain exposed only the external submit and the integration status read. `ApiKeyService.remove` also deletes by id and config without checking ownership.
blockers.resolution: The domain now resolves the integrator seat and issues and revokes keys for that account through the API Keys plugin's own `ApiKeyService` (list is a read-only projection of the plugin table filtered by the account's `referenceId` and config), never for the caller, and refuses to delete a key that does not belong to the account. Manager-only `/service/integration/account` and `/service/integration/keys` endpoints back a new account-and-keys card on the integration page (create shows the secret once, revoke confirms first). A new `GET /service/external/repairs/:id` requires the integrator role, applies the same record scope the external submit writes under, and answers an unowned or manual repair exactly as a missing one.

improvements.title: Large files written through here-document appends can be silently truncated
improvements.detail: A single missing closing delimiter leaves a syntactically invalid file, and the agent only discovers it at verification time; the warning the shell prints on stderr is easy to miss among other output.
improvements.suggestedChange: When writing files over roughly a few hundred lines, prefer the write/edit tool or write to a temporary complete file and move it into place, and treat a here-doc EOF warning as a hard failure to re-check the file before continuing.

improvements.title: The style gate reports a syntax error before the compiler does
improvements.detail: `format:auto` runs first, so a malformed TypeScript file fails as a Prettier `SyntaxError` and no later stage (typecheck, test, build) runs; the failure is reported as a build failure while the message is really a parse error.
improvements.suggestedChange: Run the type checker before the formatter (or report a formatter parse error as a type/syntax failure) so the diagnostic and the stage name agree.

improvements.title: Unit tests over pure helpers cannot catch filters that only fail when a repository compiles them
improvements.detail: Two of this round's runtime defects (the empty enum value and the datetime bound on a date column) passed every existing test because the tests never invoked the domain method against a repository; the bad value only fails inside the query builder's validator. The defects were found by running the application, not by the gate.
improvements.suggestedChange: For a domain that builds repository queries, keep at least one test that drives the method against a recording repository (asserting the emitted filter), and treat a live application probe of every list/filter endpoint as part of the standard verification for a new feature.

improvements.title: A route's `?? ''` default must be treated as absent by the domain
improvements.detail: Optional HTTP query parameters are handed to the domain as empty strings, so a domain that keys on `undefined` silently filters on an empty value for every absent parameter. The class of bug did not appear for parameters that happened to be truthy-checked.
improvements.suggestedChange: Normalise every optional string parameter with the shared `str` helper and branch on truthiness, and validate enum-valued parameters against their constant list before building the filter.

improvements.title: A `date` column needs a date-only bound; a `datetime` column needs a full timestamp
improvements.detail: The same comparison helper accepts both, but the repository's temporal validator enforces the collection's declared type, so a datetime string against a `date` field fails at query time. Inclusive comparisons should use `notAfter`/`notBefore` rather than a strict bound plus an end-of-day time.
improvements.suggestedChange: When filtering a temporal field, check the declared column type (from the migration or the generated Collection artifacts) and build the bound at that precision; prefer the inclusive operators so a value exactly on the boundary is not dropped.

improvements.title: Repair a drifted applied schema with a new conditional migration, never by replaying history
improvements.detail: When a migration file is edited after it has been applied, the recorded checksum no longer matches and the change is never replayed; `db redo` is unavailable when the applied batch also contains an irreversible migration, and `db reset` is destructive. Re-editing the file or the history table changes nothing.
improvements.suggestedChange: Add a new migration whose `up` performs only the missing delta and whose `shouldRun` checks the physical schema, so it is a no-op where the change already exists; prove it with `db apply` and leave the original file alone.

improvements.title: A capability flag and the domain rule it represents must be derived from one expression
improvements.detail: The page decides what to show from `capabilities().canUploadAttachment` while the endpoint enforces the rule in `registerAttachment`; when the two expressions were written separately they diverged and the page offered an action the domain refused.
improvements.suggestedChange: Compute the eligibility once (a named predicate shared by the capability builder and the enforcing method) so the button and the rule cannot drift.

improvements.title: A build failure makes the browser QA report a blank application rather than a build error, so the build log must be checked first
improvements.detail: All twelve round-2 browser defects described one symptom (the template homepage and a Home-only menu). The root cause was a server typecheck error that stopped pnpm build, so the production dist that pnpm start serves was stale. Treating the browser report alone would send the next agent into the page and route code.
improvements.suggestedChange: When a browser run reports a globally empty application, check the build gate output before inspecting pages; only a successful build makes a browser observation about application behavior.

improvements.title: One page id covering many settings pages cannot express a partial grant
improvements.detail: The AI plugin gates every AI settings action behind the single page `ai.settings`, which also carries manual upload and deletion. The requirement needs the supervisor to maintain the knowledge base while engineers must not upload or delete, and the only available choices were to grant the whole bundle or none of it.
improvements.suggestedChange: Let a settings provider declare its actions against finer-grained page ids (for example `ai.settings.knowledge`), so an application can grant maintenance without granting authoring.

improvements.title: The v3 runtime publishes its API base only in a served config block, so legacy consumers need a bridge
improvements.detail: `@nocobase/app-portal-sdk` reads `window.NOCOBASE_API_URL` at module load and otherwise assumes the server root, so under any non-root mount path its requests miss the base path. The v3 runtime intentionally leaves `window` untouched and exposes the base only in the `nocobase-runtime-config` JSON.
improvements.suggestedChange: Publish `NOCOBASE_API_URL` from the runtime bootstrap for plugins still on the legacy SDK, or make the SDK read the runtime-config block itself.

improvements.title: Template shell tests assert literal template copy, so a rebrand must update them without weakening the check
improvements.detail: `tests/components/layout-i18n.test.tsx` and `tests/logic/client-shell.test.tsx` asserted the template's own strings (`AI application workspace`, `Default Template v0.0.0`). Changing the application's copy failed them even though the behavior they test was intact.
improvements.suggestedChange: Have the shipped shell tests assert the keys resolve and change on language switch rather than the exact template words, so an application can rebrand without editing the tests.

improvements.title: A dialog that loads reference data must be mounted only for callers authorized to use it
improvements.detail: An always-mounted dialog fetched customers and equipment for every visitor of the list page, producing 403s for read-only roles. React mounted the dialog regardless of the server-side authorization for its action.
improvements.suggestedChange: Gate the dialog (and its loader) on the same capability that gates the action, as the list page now does for managers.

improvements.title: A locale key that holds an object is not a translation string and must not be passed to `t()`
improvements.detail: `service.workOrders.source` holds a nested object of per-source labels; a component passed it to `t()` as a React child and produced an object-child error. TypeScript cannot catch this where keys are string-typed.
improvements.suggestedChange: Reserve leaf keys for strings and give nested groups their own terminal key (as `sourceLabel` now does), and keep nested groups out of any component-visible `t()` call.

delivery.acceptanceRequirements:
每项只使用一组代表性正反场景，不展开全角色×全状态×全格式组合。浏览器 QA 验证页面行为；直接 API、并发/重复请求和服务端边界由实现阶段的针对性测试提供证据，不能用截图代替。

B01. 主管创建客户与设备，刷新后关联正确；重复设备编号、必填缺失、报修时客户设备不匹配均被拒绝。未登录者不能读取或写入业务。

B02. 普通和紧急工单各受理一次，Workflow 执行记录、对应分支说明及业务结果一致；重复受理无重复结果或通知。在测试准备提供的可控失败条件下，记录失败及恢复结果；没有该条件时仅此失败场景记未执行。

B03. 负责人开始处理、填写说明、提交确认，主管退回一次，再次提交并关闭；非法跳步和空处理说明被拒绝，已关闭只读。刷新和重新登录后状态及结果保留。

B04. 甲乙工程师只能处理自己工单；普通工单临时共享给乙后乙仅可读该单及必要关联资料，撤销后不能再读；保密工单即使被分享也不能向非负责人开放。观察员看不到内部处理备注，主管和负责人正常访问。

B05. 有阅读资格的工程师可读已发布知识但不能读草稿或修改；没有阅读资格的账号不能仅因已发布而访问。不得用管理员账户代替这组验证。

B06. 上传 PNG 和 DOCX 并保存，刷新后分别预览真实内容；一次表单校验失败保留上传选择，移除关联后不再显示。无工单权限账号通过附件链接被拒绝，损坏文件给出真实失败提示。

B07. 受理、提交确认和退回的收件人收到对应持久消息，可跳至正确工单；标记已读刷新仍保持，非收件人不能读取。无权工单链接不能因消息而绕过权限。

B08. 用受控 Scheduler 执行生成到期设备巡检和超期提醒，重复执行不重复生成同日结果，未到期/停用设备及已关闭工单不被处理；计划启停保存正确，停用后的受控调度机会不再产生新结果。负责人完成巡检并刷新核对。

B09. 主管与工程师的统计分别与各自可见列表一致；修改工单状态后数字更新，搜索和筛选不扩大权限范围。

B10. 通过既有管理入口创建并撤销集成用户密钥；独立 HTTP 测试验证报修、状态查询、重复事件去重和禁止处理/关闭，撤销或停用后调用失败。密钥全程去敏。

B11. 主管上传两份手册，页面显示真实处理状态，普通工程师不能修改库内容。条件可用时，助手能回答一条有依据问题并提供引用，对资料外问题说明不足，对无权工单拒绝泄漏；更新手册后新对话依据新内容。缺外部条件时分别报告接入完成度与真实检索/回答未验证。

B12. 助手建议进入草稿，取消不写入、明确确认后才按用户权限保存，不能自动关闭；刷新可恢复对话。模型不可用时提示真实情况，手工处理仍可用。基础业务页面切换中英文后主要文案正确，录入内容不被翻译或丢失。

实际失败记 failed，缺条件记 blocked，未执行记 not_run；不得以源码存在、已提交或静态截图冒充实际业务完成。AI 条件不足不停止其他业务搭建，也不宣称综合验收全部通过。

retro.summary: Repair round 5: the six reported failures in the after-sales service module are fixed. The work-order resolution dialog now closes on success, so Reject no longer opens a stale Submit dialog and cannot duplicate a transition. The DOCX preview is time-bounded and reports a real error instead of hanging, and a corrupt image is rejected at upload and at preview. The authenticated shell mounts the in-app notification provider with an unread bell and an authorized inbox route, and resolution and rejection now notify the people who act on them. The overdue-reminder plan scans un-closed overdue work orders, counts accepted deliveries, refuses to run while disabled, and the dialogs use the application date picker. List search filters on type, Enter and blur with a clear control. API keys are issued and revoked for the integration account through the API Keys plugin (never for the signed-in administrator), and an external self-status read was added. Scoped typecheck, eslint, Prettier and the affected service, file-preview, date-picker, locale and route tests pass.

blockers.title: operations.ts truncated mid-method by a chunked here-doc append
blockers.symptom: server/providers/service/operations.ts: SyntaxError: '}' expected. (2418:1); the file ended at `async createManual(actor: ServiceActor, input: Row): Promise` with no body or closing brace, and `format:auto` exited 2 in 0.90s.
blockers.rootCause: The implementation agent wrote the large service file through repeated `cat >> ... <<'CHUNK'` appends. One chunk was cut off (the shell logged `warning: here-document delimited by end-of-file (wanted 'CHUNK')`) and the agent's own response then hit the model output-token cap mid-thought (`stopReason: length`, thinking "Oops, my heredoc"), so the truncation was never noticed or repaired.
blockers.resolution: Read the migration and seed as the schema source of truth, removed the truncated fragment, and re-wrote the missing tail: attachment read/register/detach/resolve, manual CRUD and indexing, external-platform intake with eventId idempotency, integration status, and the dashboard/engineer-load queries. Cross-checked every `row.*`, `values.*`, `input.*` and `filter.*('col')` reference in the file against the migration's columns and fixed the remaining drifts.

blockers.title: Service code and migration disagreed on columns and column types
blockers.symptom: Latent in the same file: work orders read and wrote `acceptNoteStatus` and `acceptanceRunId` and shares read and wrote `grantedAt`, none of which existed in the migration; and `resolutionSubmittedById`/`closedById` were declared `integer` while the service and seed write the string account id.
blockers.rootCause: The truncated file was an incomplete draft, so its later methods and the migration were written at different times and were never reconciled against each other.
blockers.resolution: Added `acceptNoteStatus` (string, default `pending`), `acceptanceRunId` and `grantedAt` to the service schema migration, and changed `resolutionSubmittedById` / `closedById` to `string(64)` to match the account-id convention used by `createdById`. The migration was untracked and unmerged and had not been applied to any persistent database, so it was corrected in place; `db apply` was then run against a fresh SQLite database to confirm the schema, the six seeded work orders and the full demo data set apply cleanly.

blockers.title: The service feature is not registered, so no business page or endpoint is reachable
blockers.symptom: server/providers/index.ts and server/routes/index.ts export empty arrays, client/routes.ts declares only the home and auth pages, and there are no jobs or permission seeds. Only the migration, the seed and the six `server/providers/service/*` internals exist, so a running application shows only the homepage and the demo data is unreachable.
blockers.rootCause: The registration, route, page, job, permission and AI/Scheduler wiring were never written: the implementation agent ran out of output tokens and then its context-overflow recovery failed (`compaction_start/overflow` -> `Context overflow recovery failed`), ending the run before the remaining files were produced.
blockers.resolution: Registered the service provider (`app/service`) with permission-set creation, demo-account provisioning, acceptance-workflow materialization and Scheduler target/schedule registration; added the `/api/service/*` route module and the guarded file-repository exposure; declared the eleven client pages and their navigation group in client/routes.ts with zh/en keys; added the source-managed `work-order-acceptance` Workflow whose run modules write the acceptance note. Verified at runtime: sign-in, every list endpoint, the accept -> workflow -> note -> in-app inbox flow, attachment round-trip, and 401/403 gating.

blockers.title: Stale database schema: creating a work order returned 409 `Field "acceptNoteStatus" does not exist`
blockers.symptom: POST /api/service/work-orders answered 409 CONFLICT `Could not allocate a work-order number: Field "acceptNoteStatus" does not exist.` against the persistent development SQLite database, while every read endpoint worked.
blockers.rootCause: The applied database had been migrated from an earlier revision of `202611010001_service_schema` that predated `acceptNoteStatus` and `acceptanceRunId`; the file was edited afterwards, so its recorded checksum no longer matched its source and the already-recorded migration was not replayed. `db redo` could not repair it because the whole database is one batch containing an irreversible plugin migration.
blockers.resolution: Added the conditional corrective migration `202611010003_service_acceptance_columns`, whose `shouldRun` reads the physical table through the connection's schema inspector and only alters a database that is actually missing the columns, so it is a no-op on a fresh database. `pnpm nocobase db apply` executed it as batch 2 and the columns now exist; creating a work order returns 200. The decision is pinned by tests/logic/service-acceptance-migration.test.ts and the DDL was exercised against the real database by `db apply`.

blockers.title: Optional enum filter compared against `undefined`, so the route's `?? ''` default became an empty enum value
blockers.symptom: GET /api/service/work-orders answered an error because the domain pushed a `priority` filter built from the empty string the route passes when the query parameter is absent; the other list endpoints were unaffected because their optional strings defaulted differently.
blockers.rootCause: The domain treated the presence of the `priority` key as intent to filter and did not normalise or validate the value, while the route always supplies the key with a `?? ''` fallback. A unit test over pure helpers could not see this because it only fails when a repository compiles the filter.
blockers.resolution: `listWorkOrders` now normalises the value with the shared `str` helper and only pushes an enum filter when it is non-empty, validating against `WORK_ORDER_PRIORITIES` and returning a 400 for an unknown value. Regression cases in tests/logic/service-operations-queries.test.ts assert that the empty default pushes no filter and that an unknown priority is rejected.

blockers.title: Inspection generator bounded a `date` column with a datetime string
blockers.symptom: POST /api/service/inspections/generate answered an error / logged `Invalid date value for Field "nextInspectionDate"` instead of creating due inspection tasks.
blockers.rootCause: `generateDailyInspections` filtered `nextInspectionDate` with a `before('<planDate>T23:59:59+08:00')` bound, but the collection declares that field as `date`, and the repository's temporal validator refuses a datetime string for a date column. A `before` bound would also skip a device due exactly on the plan date.
blockers.resolution: The bound is now the date-only plan value with an inclusive `notAfter`, so a device due exactly today is included and the validator accepts the comparison. The local filter-operator interface was extended with the `notBefore`/`notAfter` operators the real builder already provides. A regression case asserts the emitted filter uses a date-only value.

blockers.title: Upload capability and domain rule disagreed about who may attach evidence
blockers.symptom: A supervisor saw the attachment upload control because `capabilities().canUploadAttachment` is enabled for a manager, but POST /api/service/work-orders/:id/attachments answered 404 `Work order #7 was not found` for that same supervisor, because the domain allowed only the assigned engineer.
blockers.rootCause: The two rules were written from one helper (`handler = isManager || isAssignee`) but the domain method applied a stricter `isAssignee` check, so the page offered an action the domain refused. The uploader is recorded in `uploaderId`, so allowing a supervisor does not attribute their upload to the engineer.
blockers.resolution: `registerAttachment` now permits the assigned engineer or a supervisor, matching the capability flag (a temporary collaborator still may not). The method comment states the rule. Regression cases cover the supervisor, the unrelated engineer and the extension check.

blockers.title: The provider called Scheduler read methods the public token type does not declare, so pnpm build failed and the browser QA saw the blank template
blockers.symptom: pnpm build failed at the Build server step with TS2339: Property 'list' / 'listOccurrences' does not exist on type 'SchedulerService' (plus implicit-any and Set<unknown> follow-on errors) in server/providers/service/provider.ts. Because the production dist was not rebuilt, the browser acceptance (NODE_ENV=production pnpm start) served a stale client, so the B01-B12 defects all reported a blank Default Template homepage with only a Home menu entry and no business pages.
blockers.rootCause: The provider imported schedulerServiceToken from the public @nocobase/app-plugin-scheduler/server/tokens entry, whose declared type only carries the registration surface (registerTarget/defineSchedule). The service actually bound to that token is the plugin's own concrete implementation, which also exposes list and listOccurrences — the same methods its management routes call — but the public declaration hides them, so the calls did not typecheck.
blockers.resolution: Described the Scheduler read surface locally (SchedulerReadService with list/listOccurrences and minimal record shapes) and cast the resolved token to it, so the reads resolve at runtime without a deep import of the plugin's unexported internal path. Confirmed with pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.server.json --noEmit (clean), a full pnpm build (Build complete), and a production pnpm start driven by headless Chrome: the sidebar shows After-sales service with Service dashboard, Work orders, Equipment, Customers, Inspections, Repair knowledge, Equipment manuals, AI service assistant and Device integration, and GET /api/service/schedules, /dashboard, /work-orders, /customers, /equipment, /knowledge all return 200 with seeded data.

blockers.title: A Workflow run module imported application tokens by relative path, so the packed artifact was not relocatable
blockers.symptom: At boot in the production build the Workflow loader threw `Cannot find module '.../storage/workflows/providers/service/tokens.js'` (node key `acceptNormal`); the run modules had been copied into the artifact store but their relative imports still pointed at the application source tree.
blockers.rootCause: The `server/workflows/work-order-acceptance/server/` run modules imported app-local code (`provider.js`, `tokens.js`) by relative path. The artifact store materializes the workflow package as a copy under `storage/workflows/<key>/<digest>`, so relative imports out of the copied package root do not resolve, and only bare-package (framework) tokens are relocatable. Materializing the app tree too would have made the artifact depend on this application's build layout.
blockers.resolution: Removed the run modules and reduced the workflow to core-only built-in nodes (a `Condition` and a `Terminate`) that contain no application imports, then moved the acceptance-note effect into the application: `ServiceOperations.runAcceptance` computes the note with a pure `acceptanceNote()` helper, calls `completeAcceptance` synchronously, and only then optionally triggers the workflow for its side effects. The effect therefore cannot be lost to a Workflow outage. The materialized artifact digest is `f8da6acfbb2b57b15a5a9c7978cdac2ccf05c13f55ed6cecbfe26789168e9d12` and the boot log reports `acceptance workflow is materialized and enabled`.

blockers.title: Enabling a Workflow by its current flag mismatched the materialized artifact, duplicating runs
blockers.symptom: The acceptance Workflow could be enabled against the source form while a different digest was materialized, so triggers either failed to find the artifact or ran alongside a stale one.
blockers.rootCause: `WorkflowService` records versions by content digest and materializes by digest; enabling via the `current` row selected a row whose digest was not the one on disk, and the development source and production build materialize different digests.
blockers.resolution: `server/providers/service/provider.ts` now enables the workflow by the exact materialized `artifact.digest` and, inside one transaction, clears the sibling `current`/`enabled` flags so exactly one version is active. The digest published in the startup log is the one that must match.

blockers.title: Work-order detail page read the wrong route parameter and requested a NaN id
blockers.symptom: Opening `/service/work-orders/1` produced `GET /api/service/work-orders/NaN` returning HTTP 400 and the page did not render the order.
blockers.rootCause: `client/pages/service/work-order-detail.tsx` read `Number(params.id)`, but the route is declared as `/service/work-orders/:workOrderId`, so `params.id` was always undefined.
blockers.resolution: Read `Number(params.workOrderId)`. The detail page now renders the order and no NaN request is issued.

blockers.title: A label used `t()` on a key that holds a translation object, so React rendered nothing
blockers.symptom: The work-order detail source label threw `Objects are not valid as a React child` (or rendered blank), because `t('service.workOrders.source')` returned the nested `source` object rather than a string.
blockers.rootCause: The locale block defines `service.workOrders.source` as an object (its values are the per-source labels), and the component passed the object to `t()` as a child.
blockers.resolution: Added a dedicated `service.workOrders.sourceLabel` string in both `client/locales/en-US.ts` and `client/locales/zh-CN.ts` and switched the component to it.

blockers.title: The AI assistant page returned 403 for every service role that could open it
blockers.symptom: `/service/assistant` rendered but the AI-employee client's `aiEmployees:list` (and `llmServices:*`, `ai:listProviderModels`) returned 403 for the manager and engineer, so the readiness surface had no data to show.
blockers.rootCause: The AI-employee plugin gates all of its settings actions behind one page grant, `{type:'page', id:'ai.settings'}`, via `requireAISettingsAccess()` in `settings-access.js`. The service permission sets granted scheduler and business pages but never `ai.settings`, and only root bypasses the check.
blockers.resolution: Granted `pageGrant('ai.settings')` to the manager permission set (the supervisor maintains the knowledge base and needs processing status) while deliberately leaving it off the engineer set, because the same page id also carries manual upload and deletion. `client/pages/service/assistant.tsx` now checks `useCan({resource:{type:'page',id:'ai.settings'},action:'access'})` and, for a caller without it, shows a supervisor-only card instead of firing the denied requests. Verified: manager `aiEmployees:list` 200 with the readiness card, engineer 403-free with the supervisor card.

blockers.title: Knowledge-base settings page failed with 404 because the legacy portal SDK resolved an API base without the mount path
blockers.symptom: `/settings/ai/knowledge-base` rendered `Unable to load this view / NocoBase request failed (404)`; the browser issued `GET /api/ai/aiKnowledgeBase:list` instead of `/main/api/ai/aiKnowledgeBase:list`.
blockers.rootCause: The knowledge-base client builds its service through the deprecated `@nocobase/app-portal-sdk`, whose `NocoBaseClient` resolves its API base at module load from `window.NOCOBASE_API_URL` and falls back to `http://127.0.0.1:13000/api`. The v3 runtime deliberately publishes nothing on `window`; the base path lives only in the served `nocobase-runtime-config` JSON (`config.api.baseURL = /main/api`).
blockers.resolution: Added `client/portal-api-url.ts` (`publishLegacyApiUrl()`), which reads the `nocobase-runtime-config` block and sets `window.NOCOBASE_API_URL`, and imported it first in `client/index.tsx` so the global exists before the knowledge-base plugin module is evaluated. Verified: the page now loads with no 404 or console error.

blockers.title: The landing page and shell still presented the template's identity instead of the application's
blockers.symptom: Browser observations reported a blank `Default Template v1.0.0-beta.50` homepage with no business menu; the sidebar footer read `AI builds freely. / NocoBase keeps it reliable.` and the header `AI application workspace`.
blockers.rootCause: The application registered its own routes and pages but never replaced the template's home component or its shell copy, so `/` was the template scaffold and the visible chrome named the template.
blockers.resolution: Rewrote `client/pages/home.tsx` into a business landing that links to every `/service/*` area, reworded `shell.workspace`/`shell.buildFreely`/`shell.reliability` to this application's wording in both locales, and made `client/layouts/components/sidebar-footer.tsx` fall back to this application's name (`t('shell.appName', {defaultValue:'Equipment after-sales service'})`) when the deployed `dist/package.json` carries no `displayName`. The two template shell tests were updated to the application's wording, keeping their mechanism assertions (language switch without remount, one active sidebar) intact.

blockers.title: Observers and engineers triggered 403s because the registration dialog mounted for callers who cannot register
blockers.symptom: On `/service/work-orders` an observer issued `GET /api/service/customers?pageSize=200` and `GET /api/service/equipment?pageSize=200`, both 403, on every page load, even though the page rendered.
blockers.rootCause: `CreateWorkOrderDialog` was always mounted and its `useLoad` fetched the customer and equipment options on mount. Registration is a manager-only action (`createWorkOrder` calls `requireManager`), so callers who hold the page only to read it were loading reference data their role is denied.
blockers.resolution: The page loads `/me` and renders the `Register` action and the dialog only when the caller's roles include `manager`. Verified: manager keeps the `New work order` button and its option load, observer and engineer see neither the button nor the dialog and issue no 403.

blockers.title: integration.tsx imported ExecutionPlansCard without using it after the plans card moved to the inspections page
blockers.symptom: eslint . --max-warnings 0 exited 1: client/pages/service/integration.tsx:70:10 error 'ExecutionPlansCard' is defined but never used. The remaining format, type and test stages still ran, so the failing gate was lint alone.
blockers.rootCause: The scheduled-plan card was moved to client/pages/service/inspections.tsx (which mounts it for managers), but integration.tsx kept the now-dead import; the file comment already stated plans live on the inspections page.
blockers.resolution: Removed the unused import from client/pages/service/integration.tsx. Scoped eslint on the file passes with --max-warnings 0 and Prettier reports the file clean; no behavior changed because the symbol was never referenced.

blockers.title: Work-order resolution dialog kept its stale label and re-posted after a success
blockers.symptom: After submitting a resolution in the same page session, 'Reject result' opened a dialog titled 'Submit resolution' and its Confirm posted to /api/service/work-orders/6/resolution, which answered 409; the close and reject dialogs also stayed open after a successful action.
blockers.rootCause: The detail page held one `dialog` state string and `act()` awaited the request but never cleared it, so the previous dialog's label and body were still bound to the open dialog and its submit handler targeted the resolution endpoint a second time. The 409 was the server correctly refusing the duplicate state transition.
blockers.resolution: `act()` in client/pages/service/work-order-detail.tsx now closes the dialog (`setDialog(null)`) after a successful action, leaving it open on failure so typed input is not lost, and then reloads the record. The open dialog therefore always matches the action the user chose and a finished transition cannot be re-submitted.

blockers.title: DOCX preview could hang on 'Loading preview' and a corrupt image was accepted without feedback
blockers.symptom: Opening a .docx attachment left the preview at 'Loading preview…' with no iframe and no error although the content request returned 200; uploading a corrupt PNG with naturalWidth 0 was accepted and produced no failure feedback.
blockers.rootCause: The Office Open XML viewer awaited the renderer and the document fetch with no time bound, so a renderer that never settled left the loading state forever with no path to an error. The image branch rendered a plain and ignored decode failure.
blockers.resolution: office-open-xml-preview.tsx now bounds both the document request (15s) and the renderer load (20s) with `withTimeout`, routing a timeout through the existing error surface, and uses a ref for `t` so the effect does not re-run on an unstable callback. file-preview-content.tsx gains an `ImagePreview` that shows a loading state, flips to a localized download fallback on `onError` or `naturalWidth === 0`, and the work-order attachment upload now rejects a zero-byte file, a photo that does not decode and a report without the ZIP `PK` signature before sending it, reporting the reason as a toast.

blockers.title: No in-app message center, unread badge, or notifications for resolution and rejection
blockers.symptom: The application had no way to open the durable in-app inbox, no unread badge in the shell, and the acceptance, resolution-submitted and rejected messages an assignee or supervisor needs could not be reached from the UI; the only inbox route was the plugin's development-only /dev page.
blockers.rootCause: The notification-in-app plugin was registered but the application never mounted its provider, declared an authenticated inbox page or put a bell in the header, and the domain only sent a notification in `completeAcceptance`: `submitResolution` and `rejectWorkOrder` changed state without telling anyone it matters to.
blockers.resolution: The authenticated shell in client/routing/app-router.tsx now mounts `NotificationInAppProvider`; a new header component reads `NotificationInAppRuntimeContext` for the unread count and links to a new authenticated, authorized `/service/messages` route that renders `NotificationInAppInbox`; the route is declared in client/routes.ts with `authz` and navigation, the page grant and page id are added to the four service permission sets, and `submitResolution` (to managers) and `rejectWorkOrder` (to the assignee) now send a durable notification through the same `notify`/`notifyManagers` path with a version-scoped idempotency key.

blockers.title: Overdue reminder plan scanned only inspections, still ran while disabled, and the date pickers closed their dialog
blockers.symptom: The overdue-reminder plan reported `reminded: 0` while overdue work orders existed; a disabled plan could still be executed through the controlled 'Run now' action; and choosing the next-inspection date or a work-order deadline with the native date input dismissed the whole dialog.
blockers.rootCause: `sendOverdueReminders` only looked at inspection tasks and counted each attempt rather than each accepted delivery, so overdue work orders were never reminded; `schedulerRunner.run` triggered the registered target without consulting `plan.enabled`; and the two dialogs used a native <input type='date'> inside a form the dialog treated as dismissible on change.
blockers.resolution: `sendOverdueReminders` scans un-closed work orders whose deadline has passed (idempotency `work-order.overdue:<id>:<day>`) in addition to the inspection half, and `notify`/`notifyAssignee` now return whether the notification service accepted the message so `reminded` counts real sends and a deduplicated delivery is not recounted. `schedulerRunner.run` refuses a switched-off plan with `status: 'skipped'`, `enabled: false` and no trigger. Both dialogs now use the application `DatePicker` (popover-based, whose button defaults to type='button') with a hidden input carrying `yyyy-MM-dd` to the FormData.

blockers.title: List search boxes did not filter until an unhandled native submit
blockers.symptom: Typing ZZZNOMATCH in the equipment or work-order list search box and pressing Enter left every row visible; the input did not filter as the user typed and had no way to clear it.
blockers.rootCause: The search input was uncontrolled and only the surrounding form's submit navigation committed it, so an Enter that did not submit the form (or a blur) never reached the query, and there was no feedback that a filter was pending.
blockers.resolution: Both list pages now use a controlled search input with a 300ms debounce, and commit on Enter (explicitly, rather than relying on form submission) and on blur; a ghost clear button resets the query and the page. Every commit resets to page 1 and updates the URL/query so the filter is durable and shareable.

blockers.title: Administrator API keys lacked the integrator role and the platform had no self-status read
blockers.symptom: A key created on the administrator's own API Keys settings page authenticates as that administrator, who holds no `service-integrator` role, so an external submit answered 403; there was no way to issue a key for the integration account; and `GET /api/service/external/repairs/:id` returned the SPA fallback because no route existed.
blockers.rootCause: The integration page told reviewers to create the key in Settings, where the plugin issues it for the signed-in administrator rather than the integration seat, and the domain exposed only the external submit and the integration status read. `ApiKeyService.remove` also deletes by id and config without checking ownership.
blockers.resolution: The domain now resolves the integrator seat and issues and revokes keys for that account through the API Keys plugin's own `ApiKeyService` (list is a read-only projection of the plugin table filtered by the account's `referenceId` and config), never for the caller, and refuses to delete a key that does not belong to the account. Manager-only `/service/integration/account` and `/service/integration/keys` endpoints back a new account-and-keys card on the integration page (create shows the secret once, revoke confirms first). A new `GET /service/external/repairs/:id` requires the integrator role, applies the same record scope the external submit writes under, and answers an unowned or manual repair exactly as a missing one.

improvements.title: Large files written through here-document appends can be silently truncated
improvements.detail: A single missing closing delimiter leaves a syntactically invalid file, and the agent only discovers it at verification time; the warning the shell prints on stderr is easy to miss among other output.
improvements.suggestedChange: When writing files over roughly a few hundred lines, prefer the write/edit tool or write to a temporary complete file and move it into place, and treat a here-doc EOF warning as a hard failure to re-check the file before continuing.

improvements.title: The style gate reports a syntax error before the compiler does
improvements.detail: `format:auto` runs first, so a malformed TypeScript file fails as a Prettier `SyntaxError` and no later stage (typecheck, test, build) runs; the failure is reported as a build failure while the message is really a parse error.
improvements.suggestedChange: Run the type checker before the formatter (or report a formatter parse error as a type/syntax failure) so the diagnostic and the stage name agree.

improvements.title: Unit tests over pure helpers cannot catch filters that only fail when a repository compiles them
improvements.detail: Two of this round's runtime defects (the empty enum value and the datetime bound on a date column) passed every existing test because the tests never invoked the domain method against a repository; the bad value only fails inside the query builder's validator. The defects were found by running the application, not by the gate.
improvements.suggestedChange: For a domain that builds repository queries, keep at least one test that drives the method against a recording repository (asserting the emitted filter), and treat a live application probe of every list/filter endpoint as part of the standard verification for a new feature.

improvements.title: A route's `?? ''` default must be treated as absent by the domain
improvements.detail: Optional HTTP query parameters are handed to the domain as empty strings, so a domain that keys on `undefined` silently filters on an empty value for every absent parameter. The class of bug did not appear for parameters that happened to be truthy-checked.
improvements.suggestedChange: Normalise every optional string parameter with the shared `str` helper and branch on truthiness, and validate enum-valued parameters against their constant list before building the filter.

improvements.title: A `date` column needs a date-only bound; a `datetime` column needs a full timestamp
improvements.detail: The same comparison helper accepts both, but the repository's temporal validator enforces the collection's declared type, so a datetime string against a `date` field fails at query time. Inclusive comparisons should use `notAfter`/`notBefore` rather than a strict bound plus an end-of-day time.
improvements.suggestedChange: When filtering a temporal field, check the declared column type (from the migration or the generated Collection artifacts) and build the bound at that precision; prefer the inclusive operators so a value exactly on the boundary is not dropped.

improvements.title: Repair a drifted applied schema with a new conditional migration, never by replaying history
improvements.detail: When a migration file is edited after it has been applied, the recorded checksum no longer matches and the change is never replayed; `db redo` is unavailable when the applied batch also contains an irreversible migration, and `db reset` is destructive. Re-editing the file or the history table changes nothing.
improvements.suggestedChange: Add a new migration whose `up` performs only the missing delta and whose `shouldRun` checks the physical schema, so it is a no-op where the change already exists; prove it with `db apply` and leave the original file alone.

improvements.title: A capability flag and the domain rule it represents must be derived from one expression
improvements.detail: The page decides what to show from `capabilities().canUploadAttachment` while the endpoint enforces the rule in `registerAttachment`; when the two expressions were written separately they diverged and the page offered an action the domain refused.
improvements.suggestedChange: Compute the eligibility once (a named predicate shared by the capability builder and the enforcing method) so the button and the rule cannot drift.

improvements.title: A build failure makes the browser QA report a blank application rather than a build error, so the build log must be checked first
improvements.detail: All twelve round-2 browser defects described one symptom (the template homepage and a Home-only menu). The root cause was a server typecheck error that stopped pnpm build, so the production dist that pnpm start serves was stale. Treating the browser report alone would send the next agent into the page and route code.
improvements.suggestedChange: When a browser run reports a globally empty application, check the build gate output before inspecting pages; only a successful build makes a browser observation about application behavior.

improvements.title: One page id covering many settings pages cannot express a partial grant
improvements.detail: The AI plugin gates every AI settings action behind the single page `ai.settings`, which also carries manual upload and deletion. The requirement needs the supervisor to maintain the knowledge base while engineers must not upload or delete, and the only available choices were to grant the whole bundle or none of it.
improvements.suggestedChange: Let a settings provider declare its actions against finer-grained page ids (for example `ai.settings.knowledge`), so an application can grant maintenance without granting authoring.

improvements.title: The v3 runtime publishes its API base only in a served config block, so legacy consumers need a bridge
improvements.detail: `@nocobase/app-portal-sdk` reads `window.NOCOBASE_API_URL` at module load and otherwise assumes the server root, so under any non-root mount path its requests miss the base path. The v3 runtime intentionally leaves `window` untouched and exposes the base only in the `nocobase-runtime-config` JSON.
improvements.suggestedChange: Publish `NOCOBASE_API_URL` from the runtime bootstrap for plugins still on the legacy SDK, or make the SDK read the runtime-config block itself.

improvements.title: Template shell tests assert literal template copy, so a rebrand must update them without weakening the check
improvements.detail: `tests/components/layout-i18n.test.tsx` and `tests/logic/client-shell.test.tsx` asserted the template's own strings (`AI application workspace`, `Default Template v0.0.0`). Changing the application's copy failed them even though the behavior they test was intact.
improvements.suggestedChange: Have the shipped shell tests assert the keys resolve and change on language switch rather than the exact template words, so an application can rebrand without editing the tests.

improvements.title: A dialog that loads reference data must be mounted only for callers authorized to use it
improvements.detail: An always-mounted dialog fetched customers and equipment for every visitor of the list page, producing 403s for read-only roles. React mounted the dialog regardless of the server-side authorization for its action.
improvements.suggestedChange: Gate the dialog (and its loader) on the same capability that gates the action, as the list page now does for managers.

improvements.title: A locale key that holds an object is not a translation string and must not be passed to `t()`
improvements.detail: `service.workOrders.source` holds a nested object of per-source labels; a component passed it to `t()` as a React child and produced an object-child error. TypeScript cannot catch this where keys are string-typed.
improvements.suggestedChange: Reserve leaf keys for strings and give nested groups their own terminal key (as `sourceLabel` now does), and keep nested groups out of any component-visible `t()` call.
